_provenance.note: tgId 17 (KEK keyLen=256, direction=encrypt/wrap, kwCipher='cipher' — the standard RFC 3394 forward-cipher construction; this release's other tgIds also cover an 'inverse' construction variant, not used here), tcId 1601, payloadLen=128 bits (16 bytes) — the group's shortest payload, i.e. RFC 3394 §2.2.1's minimum of two 64-bit blocks, and safely within this engine's own floor (rust/src/native/encrypt.rs::aes_key_wrap requires plaintext.len() % 8 == 0 && >= 16; the C++ engine's CKM_AES_KEY_WRAP path in src/lib/SoftHSM_keygen.cpp enforces the identical wrappedlen >= 16 && wrappedlen % 8 == 0 via RFC3394Pad). Independently re-verified against Python's `cryptography.hazmat.primitives.keywrap.aes_key_wrap` before use: wrapping `keyData` under `kek` reproduces `wrapped` exactly. Replaces a real-but-unprovenanced RFC 3394 §4.6 vector (had a `source` citation but no `_provenance` block, so it still failed scripts/check_acvp_provenance.py) with genuine Tier-1 NIST ACVP material per the evidence ladder in docs/remediation-plan-pkcs11-v32-coverage-2026-08-29.md §1 — ACVP-AES-KW exists, so it is mandatory over the RFC 3394 citation alone. WS-0.5 of that plan.
